how: OpenClaw's own Control UI, served by the live Gateway, opened in Google Chrome (headless, private profile) from `openclaw dashboard`'s link and operated through the Chrome DevTools Protocol with real mouse events, text insertion and key presses; <select> choices were made as Playwright's selectOption does (set the option, fire input and change). Every run was started, watched, cancelled, reloaded, viewed and downloaded from the page; no operator script started or read any run.

defects_found_by_this_acceptance_and_fix: Header read 'execution disabled' (the control plane's own flag) on a page that runs packages → 'runs available'.
Summary grid misaligned by its 'Show …' expanders; recent-run rows started with a stray separator.
Run frame always accent-red → it now takes the run's state (completed green, failed red, cancelled amber).
Tool rows said 'used only if the task needs it' for tools every run needs → precise per-tool notes.
Checklist named fields by JSON pointer → by the schema's title; untouched fields no longer shown in error.
Stop point named by node id → by the package's validated label, with the id kept.
Recent runs named a run 'live' (first string in the task) → the task's own words; tasks now keep schema order.
execution.status grew past the Gateway's 4,096-node output limit after nine runs → it returns compact summaries.
Viewing an artifact over 64 K characters, or downloading one over 48 KiB, failed with INVALID_OUTPUT → bounded views, 48 KiB chunks.
A host reporting ~35+ models would have failed the Model section → the catalog is fitted to the limit, usable models first, with a note.
